3	**Status:** Draft
4	**Owner:** Fizeau maintainers
5	**Replaces:** CONTRACT-002-ddx-harness-interface (deleted; entanglement-era contract)

7	## Purpose
8	
9	This contract defines the public Go surface of the `fiz` module. The
10	service surface is the `FizeauService` interface plus the input/output struct types
11	referenced by its methods. The only public CLI embedding surface is the
12	`agentcli` mountable command tree described below. Anything else is internal
13	and may change without notice.
14	
15	Consumers (DDx CLI, future HELIX/Dun integrations, the standalone `fiz`
16	binary, anything else) interact only through this surface. **They do not import
17	agent internal packages.** When new behavior is needed, consumers file an issue or
18	PR against this contract; agent maintainers decide whether the surface grows.
19	
20	## Module value proposition
21	
22	`fiz` is the one stop shop for automatically routed one-shot
23	noninteractive agentic prompts. Two roles:
24	
25	1. **Direct first-class agent** over native model providers (LM Studio, OpenRouter,
26	   Anthropic, etc.). Designed to be the high-performance choice for batch
27	   noninteractive tasks.
28	2. **Wrapper around other agents** — subprocess harnesses (claude, codex,
29	   opencode, pi, gemini) — used when their interactive features, vendor billing,
30	   specific capabilities, or comparison/fallback routing wants them in the
31	   candidate pool.
32	
33	A single internal routing engine ranks `(harness, provider source, endpoint,
34	model)` candidates uniformly. Consumers see one surface; the internals decide
35	how to dispatch.
36

149	## Mountable CLI Surface
150	
151	The standalone `fiz` binary and embedding callers use the same public
152	Cobra command tree from package `agentcli`:
153	
154	```go
155	package agentcli
156	
157	type MountOption func(...)
158	
159	func MountCLI(opts ...MountOption) *cobra.Command
160	func WithUse(use string) MountOption
161	func WithShort(short string) MountOption
162	func WithLong(long string) MountOption
163	func WithStdin(stdin io.Reader) MountOption
164	func WithStdout(stdout io.Writer) MountOption
165	func WithStderr(stderr io.Writer) MountOption
166	func WithVersion(version, buildTime, gitCommit string) MountOption
167	
168	type ExitError struct { Code int }
169	func ExitCode(err error) (int, bool)
170	
171	type Options struct { Args []string; Stdin io.Reader; Stdout io.Writer; Stderr io.Writer; Version, BuildTime, GitCommit string }
172	func Run(opts Options) int
173	```
174	
175	Implementation references: `agentcli/mount.go` defines `MountCLI`, mount
176	options, `ExitError`, and `ExitCode`; `agentcli/run.go` defines the non-exiting
177	`Run` runner; `cmd/agent/main.go` mounts the command and is the only
178	`fiz` command path that converts returned errors into `os.Exit`.
179	
180	Contract guarantees for embedders:
181	
182	- `MountCLI` returns a fresh, unattached `*cobra.Command` on each call.
183	- `WithUse`, `WithShort`, and `WithLong` customize help metadata without
184	  changing execution behavior.
185	- `WithStdin`, `WithStdout`, and `WithStderr` inject the streams used by the
186	  mounted root and delegated runner. Native subcommands should preserve the
187	  standalone command behavior; when a legacy implementation still writes to
188	  process streams internally, that is an implementation debt, not a license for
189	  embedding callers to parse private state.
190	- `WithVersion` supplies the version/build metadata printed by `--version`.
191	- Mounted execution never calls `os.Exit`; non-zero CLI outcomes are returned
192	  as `*ExitError`, and callers may use `ExitCode` to recover the process-style
193	  code. The standalone binary owns process termination in `cmd/agent/main.go`.
194	- Existing command paths are registered on the Cobra tree. Compatibility
195	  delegation may remain for the default prompt path and explicitly delegated
196	  commands, but migrated subcommands must not require callers to inject the
197	  `--` passthrough sentinel.

365	### Selection precedence
366	
367	> **Pin precedence is implementation reference, not the primary user surface.**
368	> Pinning `Harness`, `Provider`, or `Model` for a given prompt class indicates
369	> auto-routing is mis-deciding for that class — file a routing-quality issue.
370	> The rules below describe how the engine resolves conflicts when overrides
371	> are used; they are not how callers should normally drive `Execute`. See
372	> ADR-006 for override-tracking semantics.
373	
374	When multiple selection inputs are set on `ExecuteRequest`, they resolve in
375	the following order, most-specific first. The list is also the precedence
376	the routing engine enforces:
377	
378	1. **`Harness`** — hard pin. Routing never substitutes a different harness.
379	2. **`Provider`** — hard provider-source or endpoint pin, depending on the
380	   request surface. Routing never substitutes a different provider source or
381	   endpoint. A value that cannot be resolved fails pre-dispatch with a
382	   configuration error; no auto-substitution happens.
383	3. **`Model`** — hard pin. The request's `Model` field overrides any default
384	   model declared in the matching provider's config.
385	4. **`ModelRef`** — catalog reference. A ref to a concrete model is an exact
386	   model constraint. Catalog aliases are for exact model identity and migration,
387	   not target routing personas.
388	5. **`MinPower` / `MaxPower`** — routing strength bounds. Higher power means
389	   stronger for agent tasks. These bounds filter candidate models before
390	   scoring; they apply only to unpinned automatic routing and never override
391	   hard harness/provider/model pins.
392	
393	When no `MinPower`, `MaxPower`, exact model, provider-source/endpoint, or
394	harness constraint is supplied, automatic routing selects the best lowest-cost
395	viable auto-routable model from discovered inventory.
396	
397	Auto-selection inputs (`EstimatedPromptTokens`, `RequiresTools`, `Reasoning`)
398	apply after hard pins and power bounds. They never override an explicit pin.
399	
400	### Prompt-caching opt-out (`CachePolicy`)
401	
402	`ServiceExecuteRequest.CachePolicy` (and the mirrored `RouteRequest.CachePolicy`)
403	is the single public surface callers use to opt out of provider-side prompt
404	caching. The accepted values are `""` (interpreted as `"default"`),
405	`"default"`, and `"off"`; any other value is rejected at the service boundary
406	before any session state is opened or any provider is dispatched. The default
407	empty value means "use the per-provider default caching behavior" — the
408	concrete cache markers are stamped (or not) by the provider in a follow-up
409	bead, not by callers. Set `CachePolicy = "off"` for:
410	
411	- **Deterministic evals.** Cache hits change observed billing, latency, and
412	  occasionally the tokenizer-visible prefix; eval harnesses that need
413	  byte-for-byte reproducible attempts disable caching to remove that variable.
414	- **Privacy-sensitive prompts.** Some callers must guarantee that prompt
415	  prefixes are not retained on the provider's caching infrastructure beyond
416	  the lifetime of a single request.
417	- **One-shot benchmark runs.** Single-request benchmark scenarios pay the
418	  cache-write cost without ever realizing a hit, so disabling caching is the
419	  lower-cost and more honest measurement.
420	
421	The field is plumbed end-to-end (request → routing → provider opts) so that
422	the Anthropic `cache_control` writer (bead C) and the cache-aware cost
423	attribution path (bead D) can land without further contract churn.
424	
425	**Scope.** `CachePolicy` is request-scoped. In this contract version,
426	`ResolveRoute` MUST be observationally identical for `CachePolicy=""`,
427	`"default"`, and `"off"` — same `RouteDecision`, same ranked candidates.
428	`"off"` only suppresses provider-side cache writes (e.g. Anthropic
429	`cache_control` markers) and emits explicit-zero cache amounts in cost
430	attribution. Routing avoidance of caching-supporting vs. caching-only
431	providers is out of scope for this round.
432	
433	### Cost attribution and cache pricing
434	
435	When the configured-cost fallback prices an attempt from per-MTok rates
436	(rather than a provider-reported total), cache-read and cache-write tokens
437	are charged at the manifest's `cost_cache_read_per_m` and
438	`cost_cache_write_per_m` rates — sourced from the model entry in
439	`internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml` and projected onto
440	`telemetry.Cost.CacheReadPerM` / `CacheWritePerM`. The total
441	`CostAttribution.Amount` is the sum of input, output, cache-read, and
442	cache-write costs; the per-component cache amounts are surfaced on
443	`CostAttribution.CacheReadAmount` and `CacheWriteAmount` as `*float64`.
444	
445	The pointer-vs-zero distinction matters:
446	
447	- `nil` cache amounts mean the harness or provider did not report cache
448	  usage and no cache-rate pricing was available — the cost is unknown.
449	- An explicit zero (`*float64(0.0)`) means the caller opted out of caching
450	  via `CachePolicy = "off"`. The native loop emits explicit zero values in

450	  via `CachePolicy = "off"`. The native loop emits explicit zero values in
451	  this case so downstream consumers can distinguish "no cache activity by
452	  design" from "we have no idea."
453	
454	Historical session-log records are not retroactively re-priced; this
455	semantics applies to new runs going forward.
456	
457	Native `agent` permission modes are enforced by tool exposure at the service
458	boundary:
459	
460	- `safe` (and empty/default) exposes only read-only built-ins: `read`, `find`,

897	## Status Signal Semantics
898	
899	`ListHarnesses`, `ListProviders`, and `RouteStatus` are the status API for
900	doctor-style consumers. Consumers must not read provider-native files, auth
901	stores, quota caches, or config files directly to build routing diagnostics.
902	
903	Every normalized status datum carries:
904	
905	- `Source`: the endpoint, cache, config, or probe path that produced it.
906	- `CapturedAt`: when the service captured or read the datum.
907	- `Fresh`: whether the value is inside the service's freshness window.
908	- `LastError`: normalized `unavailable`, `unauthenticated`, or `error`
909	  information when the datum could not be captured successfully.
910	
911	Provider endpoint probes report `EndpointStatus` with reachability,
912	`ModelCount`, and `LastSuccessAt` when connected. Provider authentication is
913	reported through `ProviderInfo.Auth`; missing API keys or 401/403-style probe
914	failures are `Unauthenticated=true` and do not require consumers to know the
915	provider's native auth file format.
916	
917	`ListModels` is the public model-listing surface for configured native
918	providers. For `openrouter`, `lmstudio`, and `omlx`, it must query each
919	configured endpoint's OpenAI-compatible models endpoint (`<base_url>/models`,
920	where `base_url` normally ends in `/v1`) and return one `ModelInfo` per
921	discovered `(provider, endpoint, model)` tuple. Results carry the configured
922	provider name in `Provider`, the concrete backend type in `ProviderType`, and
923	the endpoint identity in `EndpointName` / `EndpointBaseURL`; consumers must not
924	infer these from URLs or internal config. If an endpoint is unreachable or
925	returns a non-OK response, that endpoint contributes no models and the method
926	continues listing other endpoints/providers. Missing credentials for cloud
927	providers surface through the same empty-result behavior here and through
928	`ListProviders`/`HealthCheck` status for diagnostics.
929	
930	The CLI projection for this service method is `fiz --list-models`. Its
931	JSON output must be a rendering of `ModelInfo`, including planned power-routing
932	fields as they land.
933	
934	Claude Code and Codex subscription quotas are read from durable service-owned
935	caches by `ListHarnesses`; `HealthCheck` may refresh stale caches by invoking
936	the authenticated direct PTY probe. Existing tmux-backed quota probes are legacy
937	diagnostics and must not be treated as final capability evidence. Live record
938	mode must fail immediately with a clear unavailable or unauthenticated status when the
939	target binary, credentials, or direct PTY transport dependency is missing.
940	Replay mode reads committed/generated cassette data or quota cache fixtures and
941	must not require credentials.
942	
943	`UsageWindows` are the normalized historical-usage projection. An empty slice
944	means no service-owned usage source is available for that harness/provider yet;
945	consumers should display that as unavailable rather than reading native logs
946	directly.

948	## CLI Projection Boundary
949	
950	The standalone `cmd/fiz` binary is a first-party consumer of this service
951	contract. Its job is to translate user input into public service requests and
952	render public service results. The CLI boundary is strict:
953	
954	- execution goes through `FizeauService.Execute`;
955	- session replay/follow goes through `TailSessionLog`;
956	- output decoding uses `DecodeServiceEvent` or `DrainExecute`, not local copies
957	  of private payload structs;
958	- historical session-log projections (`fiz log`, `replay`, `usage`) go
959	  through `ListSessionLogs`, `WriteSessionLog`, `ReplaySession`, and
960	  `UsageReport`; CLI subcommands do not parse session-log JSONL records
961	  directly;
962	- harness capabilities, model inventory, route feedback, quota/status, and
963	  test-only harness dispatch are consumed through public service methods.
964	
965	The CLI must not:
966	
967	- construct native providers or retry/failover wrappers;
968	- call `internal/core` loop entry points directly;
969	- synthesize service session lifecycle records into the internal session-log
970	  schema;
971	- rebuild `RouteDecision` candidate lists from config as a substitute for
972	  calling `ResolveRoute` or passing routing intent to `Execute`.
973	
974	In practice this means `cmd/fiz` must not depend on
975	`internal/core`, `internal/provider/*`, `internal/tool`, `internal/session`,
976	`internal/compaction`, `internal/harnesses`, or `internal/routing`.
977	
978	If a CLI-visible behavior cannot be expressed through `FizeauService` methods or the
979	public request/event/result types, the contract must grow first. Internal
980	package reach-through from `cmd/fiz` is architecture debt and must not be
981	normalized as a permanent compatibility layer.

983	## Catalog Power Projection
984	
985	Catalog power is service data, not consumer configuration. Consumers that need
986	to present, validate, or route by strength call:
987	
988	- `ListModels` for actual available models and their catalog `Power`,
989	  provider/deployment class, cost, speed/perf signal, context, availability,
990	  catalog reference, auto-routable state, and exact-pin-only state. The power
991	  and eligibility fields are planned in agent-da67ebbe.
992	- `Execute` / `ResolveRoute` with `MinPower` and `MaxPower` for route intent.
993	  Those request/filter fields are planned in agent-79e194aa.
994	
995	Migration rule: any consumer currently reading `~/.config/agent/models.yaml`,
996	model-catalog manifests, or hard-coded surface strings to discover power,
997	placement, or candidate policy must switch to the service methods above. Direct
998	YAML reads are allowed only inside the agent service and model-catalog
999	implementation.
1000	
1001	Catalog power is required for automatic routing. The current embedded v4
1002	manifest does not yet expose a `power` field; adding it is prerequisite work
1003	tracked by agent-735c591e and agent-91b8aa19. Initial catalog power is
1004	synthesized from normalized benchmarks such as SWE-bench and
1005	terminal/TypeScript task benchmarks when available, plus model capabilities,
1006	recency, cost, and provider/deployment class. In the absence of direct
1007	benchmark coverage, cost times recency is the default proxy within a
1008	provider/model family: the newest and most expensive model is presumed
1009	strongest unless the catalog contains an explicit override. Older family
1010	members are not auto-routable unless directly pinned or explicitly marked as
1011	useful cost/power exceptions.

1381	## Bead Execution Policy
1382	
1383	DDx bead implementation owns retry policy. The agent service selects the best
1384	candidate inside one request's power bounds, hard pins, and auto-selection
1385	inputs; it does not decide that a failed low-power attempt should become a
1386	high-power attempt. When DDx wants to escalate, it issues a new `Execute`
1387	request with a higher `MinPower`, preserving the same bead context, logs, and
1388	execution budget.
1389	
1390	DDx should normally try a low or medium `MinPower` with `reasoning=off` first,
1391	then escalate only when caller-owned evidence shows that a stronger model is
1392	likely to help. Exact `Model`, `Provider`, or `Harness` pins remain hard
1393	constraints and are not widened by escalation.
1394	
1395	Power retry is eligible when the first pass produced semantic evidence outside
1396	agent routing: model capability looked insufficient, reasoning quality was
1397	poor, post-implementation tests failed, or review blocked after the agent had a
1398	valid checkout and attempted the bead. This evidence belongs to DDx and may be
1399	submitted to the catalog/power-maintenance process, but it does not flow through
1400	agent route-health feedback and does not cause the agent to retry.
1401	
1402	Power retry is not eligible for deterministic setup failures: dirty-worktree or
1403	merge conflicts, missing repository checkout, invalid bead metadata, unresolved
1404	dependencies, config parse errors, missing harness binaries, authentication
1405	setup failures, or command-not-found/toolchain setup failures. These failures
1406	should stop with actionable evidence instead of spending a stronger attempt.
1407	
1408	Cost caps, timeout limits, permission policy, and determinism controls apply
1409	across both passes as one execution budget. The agent-side contract defines the
1410	fields and semantics; the DDx execute-loop implementation is tracked in the
1411	paired DDx repo bead `ddx-785d02f7`.
1412	
1413	## Route Attempt Feedback
1414	
1415	The agent service owns provider availability feedback for model selection.
1416	`Execute` records only the selected candidate's service-observed dispatch
1417	result: transport errors, auth/quota/rate limits, 5xx responses, stream loss,
1418	subprocess exit, timeout, malformed protocol output, and capability mismatch.
1419	These are direct signals about availability of the provider, endpoint, harness,
1420	or pinned model route.
1421	
1422	`RecordRouteAttempt` is the public feedback API for external routed work that
1423	needs to report the same availability outcomes. It is not the semantic task
1424	success/failure channel. The minimum implementation is deterministic,
1425	process-local routing feedback. The active TTL is `ServiceConfig`
1426	`HealthCooldown`; when that is unset the default is 30 seconds.
1427	
1428	Candidate keying uses the tuple `(Harness, ProviderSource, Endpoint, Model)`.
1429	Consumers should provide every field they know. A non-success `Status` with a
1430	routing-relevant `FailureClass` records an active failure and future
1431	`ResolveRoute` calls demote matching candidates inside the same process until
1432	the TTL expires. `Status="success"` clears matching active failures so a
1433	recovered candidate is eligible without waiting for TTL expiry. `RouteStatus`
1434	reports active route-attempt cooldowns on matching candidates with `Reason`,
1435	`LastError`, `LastAttempt`, and `Until` timestamps.
1436	
1437	Failure classes control what gets penalized:
1438	
1439	- `provider-transient` and `timeout` demote the provider/endpoint/model tuple
1440	  for future selections.
1441	- `capability` marks the candidate ineligible for requests needing that missing
1442	  context/tool/reasoning capability.
1443	- `setup/config`, `no-candidate`, and `cancelled` are returned to the caller as
1444	  actionable evidence but do not poison model quality. Auth/config failures may
1445	  mark a provider unusable until configuration changes, but they are not proof
1446	  that the model itself is weak.
1447	
1448	## Routing Policy Test Contract
1449	
1450	Routing tests must be statement-backed: each policy-invariant case includes a
1451	human-readable `policy_statement` so a failing assertion maps directly to a
1452	contract sentence. agent-de968c76 owns this suite. Minimum statements:
1453	
1454	- If local/free candidates are available and satisfy requested power, tools,
1455	  context, health, and hard constraints, route to local/free before paid cloud.
1456	- Local/free preference never overrides `MinPower`, `MaxPower`, exact model
1457	  pins, provider-source/endpoint pins, harness pins, or required capabilities.
1458	- A no-power request selects the best lowest-cost viable auto-routable model
1459	  from discovered inventory.
1460	- Unknown-power and exact-pin-only models are inspectable but excluded from
1461	  unpinned automatic routing.
1462	- Provider/deployment class prevents local/community benchmark ties from
1463	  equaling managed cloud frontier power solely because one benchmark is high.
1464	- `Execute` dispatches one candidate and returns route evidence; it does not
1465	  retry another candidate inside the same request.
1466	
1467	## Harness Integration Testing
1468	
1469	Real subprocess harness support uses versioned PTY cassettes as golden-master
1470	evidence. The transport decision is [ADR-002: PTY Cassette Transport for
1471	Harness Golden Masters](/Users/erik/Projects/agent/docs/helix/02-design/adr/ADR-002-pty-cassette-transport.md).
1472	The runnable replay/record workflow is documented in
1473	[Harness Golden-Master Integration](/Users/erik/Projects/agent/docs/helix/02-design/harness-golden-integration.md).
1474	
1475	ADR-002 selects direct PTY ownership inside Fizeau as the canonical service
1476	and cassette transport for live execution, record mode, replay mode,
1477	cancellation, quota probes, model-list probes, and inspection. tmux is not part
1478	of the core harness/cassette design, and tmux-only evidence must not promote a
1479	capability to final `supported` status. Replay-mode tests can prove parser,
1480	event, cleanup, timing, and transport behavior, but a harness capability is not
1481	promoted to or retained as `supported` without fresh record-mode evidence from
1482	the real authenticated harness when that capability depends on an external
1483	binary or subscription. PTY cassette record/replay is part of the `internal/pty`
1484	library boundary, with version-1 cassette timestamps quantized to 100ms by
1485	default and replay supporting realtime, scaled, and collapsed timing modes.
1486	
1487	## Behaviors the contract guarantees
1488	
1489	The agent owns these execution-time behaviors. Callers do not opt in or out.
1490	
1491	- **Orphan-model validation.** When `Model` is set but matches no provider's
1492	  discovery and no catalog entry, `Execute` fails immediately with
1493	  `Status="failed", error="orphan model: <name>"` rather than silently picking
1494	  the wrong provider.
1495	
1496	- **Discovery-backed model pins.** When `Model` is pinned and no catalog entry
1497	  exists, `Execute` resolves it through provider discovery: if `Provider` is
1498	  also pinned, only that provider's discovery is consulted; otherwise discovery
1499	  runs across all configured discovery-capable providers. If any returns the
1500	  model, the request proceeds with the catalog's no-entry cost
1501	  (`cost_source: "unknown"`) and the **provider's** default reasoning. If
1502	  discovery does not return it, the orphan-model rule above fires before any
1503	  session log is opened. Automatic routing scoring does not apply —
1504	  discovery-only models cannot be auto-selected by power bounds.
1505	
1506	- **Provider request deadline wrapping.** Every HTTP call to a provider is
1507	  wrapped with `ProviderTimeout`. Per-request failures classified as
1508	  transport/auth/upstream are reported on the final event with the attempted
1509	  route; the agent does not retry another candidate.
1510	
1511	- **Service-owned native routing and provider construction.** For the embedded
1512	  `agent` harness, `Execute` resolves configured provider candidates,
1513	  constructs the concrete provider adapter, and dispatches one candidate.
1514	  Callers express intent with `Harness`, `Provider`, `Model`, `ModelRef`,
1515	  `MinPower`, or `MaxPower`, plus the optional `EstimatedPromptTokens`/
1516	  `RequiresTools` auto-selection inputs; they do not pass provider instances,
1517	  private candidate tables, or pre-resolved `RouteDecision` values.
1518	  `ResolveRoute` results are informational only — `Execute` always re-resolves
1519	  on its own inputs (idempotent for the same caller intent, modulo health
1520	  changes).
1521	
1522	- **Route-reason attribution.** The start-event `routing_decision` and
1523	  final-event `routing_actual` together capture why each candidate was
1524	  tried/picked.
1525	
1526	- **Stall detection.** Per `StallPolicy`. Default policy (when caller passes
1527	  `nil`) uses conservative limits matching today's circuit-breaker thresholds.
1528	
1529	- **Compaction-stuck breaking.** Implicit in the `StallPolicy` default;
1530	  callers don't configure separately.
1531	
1532	- **OS-level subprocess cleanup.** On `ctx.Done()`, agent reaps PTY and
1533	  orphan processes for subprocess harnesses. Tested and guaranteed.
1534	
1535	- **Session-log persistence ownership.** When session logging is enabled,
1536	  service-owned execution writes the lifecycle and terminal records for that
1537	  session. Consumers may choose where logs are stored via `SessionLogDir`, but
1538	  they do not recreate internal session start/end records from the event
1539	  stream.
1540	
1541	- **No-op compaction telemetry suppression.** Compaction events fire ONLY
1542	  when actual work was performed. The compactor's pre-/post-turn checkpoint
1543	  probes that decide "no compaction needed" emit nothing at default verbosity.
1544	
1545	## Extensions and stability
1546	
1547	This contract is the boundary. Internal packages (`compaction`, `prompt`,
1548	`tool`, `session`, `observations`, `modelcatalog`, `provider/*`) live under
1549	`internal/` and the Go compiler blocks external imports.
1550	
1551	When a consumer needs new contract behavior, file a PR against this document
1552	proposing the addition. Maintainers decide whether the surface grows. Do not
1553	work around the boundary by importing internals (impossible after `internal/`
1554	enforcement) or by forking the module.

## Background

DDx today imports github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau (CONTRACT-003 at docs/helix/02-design/contracts/CONTRACT-003-ddx-agent-service.md). To implement Story 10's automatic escalation + reviewer pairing without DDx becoming a router (DDx must not pin Provider/Model — the spec calls that out as anti-pattern at line 374), DDx needs:

1. To know the **power** of the model that was actually dispatched, so it can request 'next call must be at least one rung stronger' via MinPower without importing catalog code into DDx.
2. To **tag** calls with what kind of work they're doing (Role) so Fizeau, telemetry consumers, and session log readers can distinguish implementer / reviewer / decomposer / etc.
3. To **link** calls that share work context (CorrelationID — e.g., 'bead_123:attempt_4') so reviewer + implementer + retry attempts can be joined in logs and aggregations.

Day 1 these are PURE observability — Fizeau's routing logic is unchanged. Future Fizeau evolution may use Role/CorrelationID for routing decisions; that's separate work, not specified by this contract change.

## What changes

ExecuteRequest gains:
- Role string — normalized: lowercased, alphanumeric+hyphen only, max 64 chars; reject invalid pre-dispatch with typed RoleNormalizationError. Empty = unset.
- CorrelationID string — normalized: printable ASCII (no control chars, no whitespace except hyphen/colon/underscore), max 256 chars; reject invalid with typed CorrelationIDNormalizationError. Empty = unset.

RouteRequest gains the same two fields with the same normalization (parity with Execute so ResolveRoute previews don't diverge).

ServiceRoutingActual gains:
- Power int — catalog-projected power value (per § Catalog Power Projection at line 983) for the actually-dispatched Model. 0 means unknown/exact-pin-only when applicable.

CONTRACT-003 reserved-cross-tool metadata keys list (today: produces_artifact, media_type) extends with:
- role
- correlation_id
Collision behavior: top-level field wins; emit MetadataKeyCollision warning event when caller also sets Metadata['role'] or Metadata['correlation_id']. Future versions may reject duplicates.

Echo behavior: Role + CorrelationID echoed into Final + RoutingDecision event.Metadata, plus session log header (one line per session). NOT echoed into per-event text_delta metadata to avoid per-token bloat (existing Metadata echo path on text_delta still applies for caller-supplied metadata that is NOT these reserved keys).

Selection precedence (line 374) is UNCHANGED for Day 1. Role and CorrelationID are observational only; they do NOT enter the precedence chain. If a future change adds routing-affecting behavior keyed on these fields, the precedence section must be amended at that time.

Routing Policy Test Contract (line 1448) gains minimum statements:
- Role + CorrelationID are echoed into RoutingDecision + Final events
- Role + CorrelationID are echoed into the session-log header
- Role + CorrelationID are NOT echoed into text_delta event metadata
- Role + CorrelationID never affect eligibility filtering Day 1
- Without a CorrelationID, routing is unchanged from baseline
- ResolveRoute and Execute observe identical routing policy for the same correlation-aware request (Day 1: both ignore for routing)
- Invalid Role / CorrelationID values rejected pre-dispatch with the typed errors
- ServiceRoutingActual.Power reflects the catalog-projected power of the dispatched Model
- When caller sets both top-level Role and Metadata['role'], top-level wins and a MetadataKeyCollision warning is emitted

## What this enables downstream (informational)

DDx will use these fields to:
- Compute next-attempt MinPower from previous.RoutingActual.Power + rung_step (cost-tier escalation)
- Tag implementer + reviewer calls with Role for telemetry; share CorrelationID for trace-join
- Set MinPower = implementer.RoutingActual.Power + 1 on the reviewer call (best-effort 'more powerful'); 'different provider' is best-effort emergent, not promised
- When same-provider results on review, log a degradation event for operator visibility

DDx will NOT:
- Pin Provider/Model
- Implement any tiebreaker keyed on CorrelationID
- Define role-specific routing policy

## Out of scope

- Role-specific Fizeau routing policy (config registry, per-role defaults, etc.)
- Correlation-aware routing intelligence (tiebreakers, diversity bias, learned preferences)
- Multi-tenant correlation namespacing
- Cancellation semantics for any future correlation state
- DDx→Fizeau outcome-feedback API
- Anything keyed on Role or CorrelationID that affects routing
